source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Bed rails, bedside tables, call controls, doorknobs, commodes, and nearby equipment.","B":"Ceiling tiles, upper wall corners, and light fixtures.","C":"Prioritize floors and lower wall surfaces because they accumulate the greatest environmental bioburden during routine care.","D":"Windows and ceiling vents unless blood or body fluid is visible."}}
source_row.rationale: Frequently touched surfaces close to the patient accumulate repeated hand contact and are more likely to participate in contact transmission. CDC specifically highlights bedrails, bedside tables, commodes, doorknobs, sinks, and nearby equipment for appropriate routine cleaning and disinfection.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Isolation Precautions — Environmental Measures: prioritize cleaning/disinfection of frequently touched surfaces near the patient such as bedrails, bedside tables, commodes, doorknobs and nearby equipment. Current CDC isolation-precautions guidance at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control; Reporting of Incident/Event and infection/safety activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Environmental services is prioritizing cleaning in a room occupied by a client with frequent staff contact. Which surfaces should receive particular attention as high-touch surfaces?
